title: `is_resource()` no longer detects DBA, ODBC, and SOAP handles
summary: As of PHP 8.4, dba_open()/dba_popen(), odbc_connect()/odbc_pconnect(), odbc_prepare()/odbc_exec() and related ODBC functions, and the SoapClient::$httpurl/SoapClient::$sdl properties return objects instead of resources, so any surviving is_resource() guard silently returns false for a perfectly healthy value and takes the error branch on success; the correct replacement check is false for the DBA and ODBC values but null for the two SOAP properties specifically, and the two must not be conflated.
new_code_policy: On a PHP 8.4+ floor, never guard the return value of dba_open(), dba_popen(), odbc_connect(), odbc_pconnect(), odbc_prepare(), odbc_exec(), or any other ODBC result-producing function with is_resource(); check it against false instead (`$handle !== false`). For SoapClient::$httpurl and SoapClient::$sdl specifically, check against null (`$client->sdl !== null`), never against false and never with is_resource() - those two properties are an object or null, never false.
existing_code_policy: Search a codebase for every is_resource() call that touches a DBA, ODBC, or SOAP value - dba_open()/dba_popen() results, odbc_connect()/odbc_pconnect() connections, odbc_prepare()/odbc_exec()-family results, and the SoapClient::$httpurl/SoapClient::$sdl properties - and replace each with the check that matches its own source API, not one blanket substitution: DBA and ODBC values become `!== false` checks, because false was already their failure sentinel before PHP 8.4 and remains so after it, while the two SOAP properties become `!== null` checks specifically, because UPGRADING documents them as the stated exception to the false rule. Trace each is_resource() call back to where its argument actually came from before choosing a replacement - a shared helper function, or a variable that could carry a DBA handle down one call path and a SOAP property down another, cannot be fixed with a single mechanical rewrite across the whole codebase.
guideline: Do not use is_resource() to test whether a DBA, ODBC, or SOAP handle is open, on a PHP 8.4+ floor: check DBA and ODBC values against false, and check SoapClient::$httpurl and SoapClient::$sdl against null instead - the two are not interchangeable, and using the same replacement for both gets one of them wrong.
details: PHP 8.4 turned several long-standing resource types into objects (UPGRADING-8.4.0, "1. Backward Incompatible Changes" -> "Resource to Object conversions"): dba_open() and dba_popen() now return a Dba\Connection instead of a resource; odbc_connect() and odbc_pconnect() now return an Odbc\Connection, and odbc_prepare(), odbc_exec(), and various other ODBC functions now return an Odbc\Result; and SoapClient::$httpurl and SoapClient::$sdl are now Soap\Url and Soap\Sdl objects rather than resources. is_resource() returns false for every value that is not an actual resource - including a perfectly healthy object - and raises no diagnostic of any kind when handed one (confirmed locally on PHP 8.4.19: is_resource() on a plain object and on null both return false silently, with an active error handler installed and nothing reported). So a guard written as `if (!is_resource($handle))` or `if (is_resource($handle))`, which used to distinguish an open handle from a failed one on PHP 8.3 and earlier, now takes the "failed" branch every single time it runs on PHP 8.4+, even when the connection, statement, or WSDL parse succeeded outright: the check silently and permanently fails closed, and because the resulting error path is usually a generic "could not open/connect" exception, the failure looks exactly like a real connection problem with nothing pointing at the actual cause. UPGRADING-8.4.0 states the general rule - "Return value checks using is_resource() should be replaced with checks for `false`, unless specified otherwise" - and then immediately specifies otherwise for the two SOAP properties: SoapClient::$httpurl and SoapClient::$sdl "should be replaced with checks for null", not false. This is because, unlike the DBA and ODBC functions (which already returned false on failure before PHP 8.4, so `!== false` is simply the typed equivalent of the old check), these two SOAP properties were never false-on-failure to begin with: they hold an object on success or are left null when there is nothing to report (for example, no WSDL was parsed), so null is, and always was, their absent-value sentinel. Treating all five affected APIs the same way and mechanically replacing every is_resource() with a false-check gets the DBA and ODBC cases right and silently gets the SOAP case wrong. Because this change spans three unrelated extensions - DBA, ODBC, and SOAP - with nothing extension-specific about the fix itself, no single `extension` value would be accurate for this rule; what is actually actionable is the is_resource() idiom, which is a Core function, so this rule is filed as `core` rather than under any one of the three extensions it touches.

before: throw new RuntimeException('Unable to open DBA database: ' . $path);
after: throw new RuntimeException('Unable to open DBA database: ' . $path);

before: throw new RuntimeException("Unable to connect to ODBC data source: {$dsn}");
throw new RuntimeException('ODBC query failed: ' . odbc_errormsg($connection));
after: throw new RuntimeException("Unable to connect to ODBC data source: {$dsn}");
throw new RuntimeException('ODBC query failed: ' . odbc_errormsg($connection));

before: throw new RuntimeException('SOAP client has no parsed WSDL definition.');
after: throw new RuntimeException('SOAP client has no parsed WSDL definition.');

notes: is_resource() returns false unconditionally for any value that is not an actual resource, and raises no notice, warning, or deprecation of any kind when handed one - confirmed locally on PHP 8.4.19 with an active error handler installed: is_resource(new class {}) and is_resource(null) both return false with nothing reported. This is exactly why a stale guard fails silently and indistinguishably from a real connection failure once its argument becomes an object instead of a resource.

The DBA, ODBC, and SOAP extensions are not installed in this verification environment (`php -m` lists none of dba, odbc, or soap, and function_exists('dba_open'), function_exists('odbc_connect'), and class_exists('SoapClient') all report false here), so the affected functions and SoapClient itself could not be executed or have their return types inspected directly in this environment. The API-level facts above - which functions and properties are affected, and which of them require a false-check versus a null-check - are drawn directly from the pinned UPGRADING-8.4.0 source text quoted below, not from local execution.

A mechanical, codebase-wide replacement of is_resource($x) with $x !== false is unsafe: it is correct for DBA and ODBC handles but silently wrong for SoapClient::$httpurl and SoapClient::$sdl, which UPGRADING specifies as checks for null instead - and a text-level rewrite has no way to know, from the shape of `is_resource($x)` alone, which of the three extensions actually produced $x, especially once $x has passed through a shared helper function or several layers of code before reaching the check. This is why behavior_change_risk is "high" and why a no-automatic-replacement example is included alongside the three illustrative ones above: a stale guard fails closed while looking exactly like an unrelated connection error, with no diagnostic anywhere pointing at the actual cause.

PHPCompatibility 10.0.0-alpha2 produced no finding - confirmed via `phpcs --standard=PHPCompatibility --runtime-set testVersion 8.2-8.5` against probe code exercising is_resource() guards on dba_open(), odbc_connect(), odbc_exec(), SoapClient::$sdl, and SoapClient::$httpurl - for any of these constructs at testVersion 8.2-8.5, so there is no proven sniff mapping for this rule; verification.phpcompatibility is intentionally empty rather than guessed.

Evidence: UPGRADING-8.4.0.txt, "1. Backward Incompatible Changes" -> "Resource to Object conversions": "Return value checks using is_resource() should be replaced with checks for `false`, unless specified otherwise." DBA: "dba_open() and dba_popen() will now return Dba\Connection". ODBC: "odbc_connect() and odbc_pconnect() will now return Odbc\Connection", "odbc_prepare(), odbc_exec(), and various other functions will now return Odbc\Result". SOAP: "SoapClient::$httpurl is now a Soap\Url object rather than a resource. Checks using is_resource() (i.e. is_resource($client->httpurl)) should be replaced with checks for null (i.e. $client->httpurl !== null)." and the equivalent line for SoapClient::$sdl / Soap\Sdl.
